chunks: From him, from one of his companions, from Husayn ibn 'Umara, from Husayn ibn Abu Saeed Al-Mukari and Jahm ibn Abu Jahma, from Abu Ja'far, a man from the people of Kufa who was known by his teknonym, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Teach me a supplication I can use to supplicate with.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, say: O the One I hope for every goodness, and O the One whose wrath I feel safe from at every stumble, and O the One Who gives much for a little, O the One Who gives to the one who asks Him out of His compassion and mercy, O the One Who gives to the one who does not ask Him and does not know Him! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and give me, due to my asking, from all the goodness of the world and all the goodness of the Hereafter, for it is not deficient what You have given me, and increase me from the expansiveness of Your grace, O Generous!'
ai.seo_question: What is a comprehensive supplication for all worldly and hereafter needs taught by the Imams?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia theological emphasis on divine generosity (al-Karim) and the concept that God’s gifts are never deficient (ghayr manqūṣ). It serves as a comprehensive invocation for both worldly and spiritual needs, reflecting the Imam’s role in guiding believers to articulate their hopes through attributes of mercy and abundance.
